title: Tech giants are getting caught in a compute conundrum
excerpt: Microsoft has had a tough year on the stock market, with its cloud business being a blessing and a curse.
content_html:
The past 12 months have not been kind to Microsoft.

Once the most valuable company in the world, the Big Tech titan's share price has been sliding. Microsoft's stock dropped 19% in June, its worst month since the dot-com crash. Some of its top brands, like Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Xbox, are facing serious headwinds and questions about their future.

BI's Ashley Stewart, our resident Microsoft expert, broke down how the tech giant is trying to mount a comeback on multiple fronts.

It wasn't always this way. A few years ago, Microsoft was the top dog, getting praised for its foresight on the AI revolution. An early investor in OpenAI, Microsoft also quickly implemented AI into its search engine, Bing.

AI's volatility is bound to swing companies' fortunes quickly, but it's hit Microsoft particularly hard. Its 12-month stock performance (down roughly 25%) is the worst of the Magnificent Seven by a decent margin. (Meta is the next closest, down almost 17%.)

Microsoft will get another test on Wednesday when it reports earnings after the bell.

At the heart of Microsoft's challenge is a classic business dilemma: Does it cash in on demand today or focus more on its long-term goals?

Compute is the name of the AI game. Microsoft has the benefit of a massive cloud business in Azure that can help customers meet those needs.

But Microsoft's cloud business is a gift and a curse. There is only so much compute to go around, and Microsoft has its own AI plans it needs that infrastructure for.

That means a decision: Allocate those resources toward its clients or itself?

The former leads to the more immediate boost to the top line, but comes with a risk. Less compute for Microsoft means fewer resources to develop and run its products, which could set it further back in the AI race.

Keeping more compute for itself is a bet that Microsoft's products will ultimately take off, which is good for the long run. But disappointing growth for Azure could tank its stock immediately.

This isn't happening in a vacuum. Google Cloud continues to put up massive numbers. (Although it's also feeling the pinch of AI spend as its free cash flow went negative for the first time in decades.)

And while they're not as complete an offering as Azure, Meta and SpaceX are also getting in the compute-for-hire game.

So as Microsoft continues to debate how it wants to split up its compute, its customers have alternatives. And they might not stick around to find out what Microsoft decides.

Dan DeFrancesco

content_html_zh:
过去 12 个月对微软来说并不好过。

这家曾经是世界上最有价值的公司的大型科技巨头的股价一直在下滑。 6 月份微软股价下跌 19%，这是自互联网泡沫破灭以来最糟糕的一个月。 它的一些顶级品牌，如 Microsoft 365、Copilot 和 Xbox，正面临着严重的阻力和对其未来的疑问。

BI 的阿什利·斯图尔特（Ashley Stewart）是我们的微软常驻专家，他详细分析了这家科技巨头如何试图在多个方面卷土重来。

情况并非总是如此。 几年前，微软是领头羊，因其对人工智能革命的远见而受到赞誉。 作为 OpenAI 的早期投资者，微软也很快将人工智能应用到其搜索引擎 Bing 中。

人工智能的波动必然会迅速改变公司的命运，但它对微软的打击尤其严重。 其 12 个月的股票表现（下跌约 25%）是七大公司中表现最差的，幅度相当可观。 （Meta 是第二接近的，下降了近 17%。）

微软将在周三盘后报告财报时接受另一次测试。

微软面临的核心挑战是一个典型的商业困境：它是按需兑现还是更多地关注其长期目标？

计算是人工智能游戏的名称。 Microsoft 拥有 Azure 中庞大的云业务的优势，可以帮助客户满足这些需求。

但微软的云业务既是礼物也是诅咒。 可供使用的计算量是有限的，而微软有自己的人工智能计划，它需要该基础设施。

这意味着一个决定：将这些资源分配给客户还是自己？

前者可以更直接地提高收入，但也存在风险。 对于微软来说，更少的计算意味着更少的资源来开发和运行其产品，这可能会使其在人工智能竞赛中进一步落后。

为自己保留更多的计算能力是微软产品最终会起飞的赌注，从长远来看，这有好处。 但 Azure 令人失望的增长可能会立即导致其股价下跌。

这不是在真空中发生的。 谷歌云继续提供大量数据。 （尽管它也感受到了人工智能支出的压力，因为其自由现金流几十年来首次出现负值。）

虽然 Meta 和 SpaceX 的产品不像 Azure 那样完整，但他们也开始涉足租用计算领域。

因此，当微软继续争论如何拆分其计算时，其客户有其他选择。 他们可能不会留下来看看微软的决定。
